title: Chicken Pot Pie
ingredients: 1 pound skinless, boneless chicken breast halves - cubed
instructions: Gather all ingredients. Preheat the oven to 425 degrees F (220 degrees C).
Combine chicken, carrots, peas, and celery in a saucepan; add water to cover. Bring to a boil; boil for 15 minutes. Drain.
Meanwhile, melt butter in a separate saucepan over medium heat. Add onion; cook until soft and translucent, 5 to 7 minutes. Stir in flour, salt, black pepper, and celery seeds.
Slowly stir in chicken broth and milk.
Reduce heat to medium-low; simmer until thick, 5 to 10 minutes. Set aside off heat.
Place 1 crust in a 9-inch pie plate; add chicken and vegetables to the crust. Pour hot broth mixture over top.
Cover pie with top crust, seal the edges, and trim any excess dough. Make several small slits in top crust to allow steam to escape.
Bake in the preheated oven until pastry is golden brown and filling is bubbly, 30 to 35 minutes. Cool for 10 minutes before serving.

most_helpful_positive_review.text: The first time I made this I followed the recipe to the letter and thought it tasted great but was too dry. So I doubled the sauce, used a deep dish pie plate, reduced the temp to 375 & baked for 45 minutes. It was perfectly moist without being runny, and the pie shells were perfectly done. Absolutely fabulous! Goes without saying it is a keeper!

featured_tweaks.text: This is five stars but you need to add 1/4tsp of garlic powder and 1/2 tsp of poultry seasoning like another reviewer suggested. This adds that missing flavor. Also I baked the bottom pie shell for 7 minutes and then added the filling. Overall yummy yummy!

This is definitely the best chicken pot pie I'd ever had...who would believe a made-from-scratch one would be so easy! DELICIOUS. Whole family loved! I took a couple suggestions from other reviews and added diced baked potato, used mixed canned veggies and baked the bottom crust for 5 min. prior to adding the filling. Thanks for the recipe!

I made this with some tweaks. I prefer a more herb tasting pie and more seasoning in general. As others, I increased the broth/gravy mixture, but only by 50%, not double as some have done.

I sauteed the chicken cubes in butter with the onion and added a 1/4 cup of chopped Baby Bella mushrooms. I added the salt, black pepper, poultry seasoning, and crushed thyme to this mixture at the end of the saute, In addition to the chopped celery, sliced carrots, frozen peas, I added 2 small chopped yellow skinned potatoes and sauteed them in a separate pan with 1/3 cup butter.

When the veggies were tender but firm, I added the veggies to the chicken. Then added the flour, chicken broth and half and half for the milk.

I increased the broth/gravy by about 50%. I baked at 375 degrees for 45 mins. If not brown enough, turn up to 425 for 5 mins to finish. Nice, have made twice!

I have made this recipe many times over the years and my family loves it! I always appreciate the helpful changes that people share so I thought I might share mine now that I found the mixture that my family prefers .First, we are crust lovers so I make mini loaf pies so everyone has a complete upper and lower crust. I make the following changes to the recipe to make 10 mini loafsThe ingredientsI use that are a bit different :10 miniloaf pans2 lbs of chicken breast4 packages of premade pie crusts1- 10 oz bag frozen peas1 - 10 oz bag of frozen green beans1 -10oz bag of frozen corn1 -bag of shredded carrots3 - 32 oz chicken broth boxes8 - medium size gold potatoes2 tablespoons of crushed garlicFollow the recipe as directed except I boil chicken and vegetables in chicken broth instead of water. Save broth after draining . I use this broth to boil the potatoes as well as using it in the cream sauce.Cook potatoes until tender in the drained broth. Drain and save broth and add potatoes to the drained chicken and vegetable mixture.Triple the cream sauce recipe but cook as directed. In addition to the onion, sautee the garlic for the last minute . Use some of the broth that was drained from vegetables and potatoes as the broth for the cream sauceThese modification enough filling for 10 mini loaf pot pies (and usually a little bit extra).

As a BASE recipe, this is fine. However, there are definitely not enough seasonings in this recipe, so double (or triple) to taste and add whatever savory seasonings you'd add to a chicken soup (sage, poultry seasoning, whatever you have that would go well with a cream sauce). I made this as is out of curiosity and it was SO bland. We changed a few things about this recipe and we loved it! 1. I increased the butter/flour to 1/2 cup each so I didn't have that annoying bit of butter left over. Since you're going to have more roux, increase the chicken stock to 2 cups and the milk to 1 cup. 2. I did not boil the filling (chicken and veggies) in water. Why boil it in water, drain away some of the nutrients, and then add in chicken stock? I boiled it in enough chicken stock to cover, adding the seasonings while it cooked, removed after it was cooked through, strained it into a large measuring cup, and then used that cooking liquid as the chicken stock for the gravy. I did have a little more stock than I needed, but the leftovers would make a great base for ramen or a smaller serving of soup. 3. I cooked the roux a little longer, until it smelled nice and nutty. 4. MIX THE CHICKEN, VEGGIES, AND GRAVY BEFORE YOU PUT IT IN THE PAN. Just pouring the gravy over the veggies is going to leave dry spots and if you try to mix it up, you risk tearing the pie crust dough. just toss the filling in with the gravy, mix it all up, and scoop it out into the crust. 5. If you don't feel like making an actual pie, you can always cook the filling a little longer (temp check your chicken), do everything up to the gravy, throw some biscuits in the oven and make inside out chicken pot pie :)

Boil chicken celery peas and carrots ?? No thank you. Boiling away flavor and nutrients. Dice and cook chicken in skillet with a 1T olive oil( added 1t italian seasoning a clove of garlic and 1/2 t sage) set aside. Meanwhile steam carrots, when almost done add peas. In same skillet cook onions,celery follow directions from there.

I use this recipe mainly for the sauce and take some major shortcuts. I use Marie Callender's frozen pie crust, half a rotisserie chicken and frozen mixed vegetables. I take out the pie crust to thaw a bit while I make the sauce (as directed). After the sauce thickens a bit, I add about 2 cups frozen mixed vegetables. I cube the rotisserie chicken and throw it in the same pot and mix everything up. It's the perfect consistency. I then pour it all into the pie crust. Then I take the other pie crust (2 come in a box) and gently lay it on top. It's important that they're thawed a bit so you can pinch them together. So easy and delicious.

I do absolutely LOVE this recipe. I have made it at least a couple dozen times and have learned a couple of things along the way. 1. Bake your bottom crusts for 5-7 minutes first to prevent a "soggy bottom". 2. Make extra sauce, increase the ingredients by 50%, this will prevent it from being dry. 3. Add the fillings and sauce in layers, the sauce is thick, and does not settle to the bottom 4. Use a whole-egg egg wash on the crust to help seal the crust and gives it that professional look and flaky crust. TIP: If you have extra sauce or filling you can use it to add more sauce to your slice later of make a bit of chicken pot pie soup!

Great recipe! I just did a few tweaks for my own liking. I doubled the gravy, added a few more veggies and few small cubes of potatoes.I browned all vegetables with the onion, butter and I added some garlic, parsley, sage, and rosemary. On a side-note…I learned from a professional Baker, that she used the boxed JIFFY PIE CRUST, it makes the best crust! Freeze it for 10 minutes in pie plate before you add your filling and it will bake so flaky! I also use individual glass pie plates. I feel the distribution of everything is more controlled.😊

First of all, I think using another pie shell as the top of the potpie is GENIUS. I've been making chicken potpie for years, and I never thought of doing that. I do, however, have some major modifications to the dish, which, to me, make it a SIX STAR dish! First, I would cook potatoes, carrots and the chicken in chicken stock. I would add frozen corn near the end of he cooking process. Then drain the stock and put into a saucepan. I would thicken with a bit of Wondra flour and a little butter, That would all be poured over the meat and veggies in the pie shell. I would check for seasoning and place the top shell. Then, brush the top crust with some melted butter and place on a baking sheet. Bake 350 degrees for about 45 minutes. TERRIFIC flavor. The secret is to make that liquid as much like chicken gravy as possible.
